correctness.rationale: For the stipulated labels 0,1,2,3, the leaf condition forces each pair to cost at least two, with (cycle,leaf)=(0,2) the only equality case. If a center and both immediate cycle neighbors are equality pairs, the center has closed-neighborhood sum two and is invalid. Thus the exceptional indices meet all n centered cyclic triples, each exceptional index serving exactly three centers; at n=3 identical sets of vertices still count as three distinct centers. The lower bound is 2n+ceil(n/3). For the upper bound give every leaf label 2 and the cycle the word (100)^q followed by nothing, 1, or 10 for residues 0, 1, or 2. In each case every centered cyclic triple contains one or two ones, so the closed sum is exactly 3 or 4 at each cycle vertex. There is no restriction at a leaf labeled 2. This verifies all n≥3 under the specified closed-neighborhood condition, not an open-neighborhood variant.
residual_risks: No fresh execution of the uploaded script. Its full-label loop visits every candidate at n=3,4,5 but skips feasibility checks above the current best; this is sound for the minima and is not a census of all feasible assignments. The finite checks do not prove the arbitrary-order result.

value.rationale: The cycle with one leaf at each vertex is a canonical unicyclic corona, not an arbitrary finite instance. The answer is an all-orders exact benchmark for the perfect double Italian constraint and identifies the one-extra-unit-per-three-positions obstruction. A researcher comparing ordinary, restrained and perfect variants can use the exact number where the related formulas do not determine it.
residual_risks: No extension to arbitrary coronas or to an exact-open-sum variant is claimed.
